en.title: Gender of nouns
en.summary: English nouns have no grammatical gender; the pronouns he, she and it show natural gender.

paragraphs: Many languages give every noun a grammatical gender, such as masculine or feminine. English does not. Its nouns have no gender, and the articles and adjectives never change for it. Gender appears only in the pronouns he, she and it, and it follows the real sex of the person.

A few nouns for people have separate male and female forms, such as actor and actress, or host and hostess. Today many speakers prefer a single neutral word for both. Names of jobs are often neutral already: teacher, doctor, singer.
We usually call animals and things it. We use he or she for a pet or a farm animal we know well. Ships and countries were once called she, but this use is old-fashioned.
When the person's sex is unknown or irrelevant, we use they: Someone called, and they left a message. This singular use of they is common in speech and is accepted in most modern writing.

items: Wrong: **The table is beautiful, she is old.** Right: **The table is beautiful, it is old.**
Wrong: **a beautiful woman doctor lady** Right: **a woman doctor**
Wrong: **The sun, he is hot.** Right: **The sun is hot.**

ro.title: Genul substantivelor
ro.summary: În limba română, fiecare substantiv are un gen: masculin, feminin sau neutru.

paragraphs: Substantivul este cuvântul care denumește o ființă sau un lucru. În limba română, toate substantivele au un gen gramatical. Genurile sunt masculin, feminin și neutru.
Aflăm genul când numărăm substantivul la singular și la plural. La masculin numărăm cu: un, doi. La feminin numărăm cu: o, două. La neutru numărăm cu: un, două.
